entries.note: A sweeping denunciation of the bubble and its promoters, without a determinate factual test.
Judges the usefulness of run rates and the quality of journalism.
The central assertion concerns usefulness and informational value, without specifying a predictive or accounting test.
The accounting comparison is hedged with 'It appears.' The source does not identify the ethical explanation as OpenAI's own explanation.
Calling reporting a marketing exercise is an evaluative characterization in this passage.
An insult directed at investors who use the metric.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures and reporting available at publication would establish whether these AI revenue figures were known and whether Microsoft's only available annual figure was Bloomberg's fiscal 2026 estimate.
entries.note: This concerns the public availability of figures, not whether the companies internally know them.
The surrounding discussion concerns 2026 revenue; 'a year' loses that horizon. The revenue estimate is explicitly 'likely,' and the leaking assertion is counterfactual.

entries.test: Customer revenue concentration disclosures, customer identities, subscription terms and token usage costs would establish whether the dominant customers are predominantly AI startups offering the described subsidies.
entries.note: 'From what I hear' identifies his evidentiary basis while retaining the factual assertion.

entries.test: Harvey's and other AI startups' service costs, customer payments and responses to cost-covering prices would test the claimed universal inability to sustain customer demand at those prices.
entries.note: He explicitly links customers' unwillingness to cover costs to the absence of product-market fit. The surrounding text supplies a cost-based meaning for that term.

entries.test: OpenAI's and Anthropic's customer revenue distributions, customer classifications and those startups' revenue and token expenditures would test the stated percentages.
entries.note: The precise concentration and spending claims are testable even if the necessary disclosures are currently unavailable.

entries.test: AI startup financial statements, cash flows and financing histories would establish whether all operate at losses that require large capital raises every few months.
entries.note: A profitable or self-financing AI startup could refute the universal assertion.

entries.test: Revenue and customer token spending around successive model releases would establish whether every release causes a substantial startup-funded revenue increase for OpenAI and Anthropic.
entries.note: This asserts an existing recurring causal pattern.

entries.test: AI startup supplier relationships, token costs, customer prices and demand at cost-covering prices would test whether every startup subsidizes OpenAI or Anthropic tokens because customers will not cover their cost.
entries.note: The extraction metaphor accompanies concrete universal claims about resale economics.
Attributes a deliberate private purpose to the companies' financial opacity.

entries.test: SiliconData's index methodology, input data and weighting would establish whether spot pricing overwhelmingly dominates long-term contract prices.
entries.note: The index-composition assertion is Zitron's own, despite the imagined objection introducing it.

entries.test: The contracts and reports he cites, compared with contemporaneous quoted GPU rental rates, would establish whether multiple companies paid substantially less.
entries.note: The subsequent examples give 'supposed going rate' a concrete benchmark.

entries.test: The Canopy Wave contract rates and duration, together with GPU acquisition costs and the stated six-year depreciation assumption, would settle the hourly depreciation and revenue-share calculation.
entries.note: The mismatch between a six-year depreciation period and a five-year contract is present in the original.

entries.test: Public capacity disclosures, procurement agreements and operational data available at publication would establish whether evidence supported at least one gigawatt of compute available to Anthropic.
entries.note: The 5GW forecast is attributed to investor statements reported by the Times; Zitron's own assertion concerns the supporting evidence.
There is no shared criterion for counting stacked assumptions or determining when they 'fall apart' across this broad body of writing and investment.
The central characterization of what is understood as 'extremely grim' is evaluative.

entries.test: Hyperscaler and AI lab customer revenue breakdowns, together with the labs' and startups' cash flows and financing requirements, would test the asserted revenue concentration and funding dependence.
entries.note: The plain reading is that these customers supply an overwhelming majority of revenue and require continuing external financing.

entries.test: Monthly AI startup token spending and OpenAI and Anthropic revenue data would test whether either lab can grow during periods when startup spending fails to increase.
entries.note: The indefinite-time flourish does not erase the concrete claim that growth requires startup spending to rise every month.
An exaggerated characterization of media optimism rather than a defined content-analysis claim.
The normalization broadens 'every deranged, multi-faceted model' to every complex model. The original is a polemical dismissal of financial modeling.
A denunciation and investment warning without a determinate test for its personal classifications or claimed protection from losses.
